profile.name: Alex Ababu
profile.statement: I build AI that's useful, not just impressive: end-to-end systems, evaluated honestly, secured properly, and as simple as the problem allows.

about.heading: AI Engineer, grounded in software engineering.
body: My background is software engineering, mostly in fintech. At Huawei and Arifpay Financial Technologies, I built and redesigned payment infrastructure used by 20+ financial institutions, worked as a solutions architect on a large-scale mobile money platform, and took on freelance projects along the way.

Now I build AI-powered software: business process automation and agentic AI solutions that start from a business or customer need and end with something that makes the process faster, cheaper, and better. I recently finished a Master's in AI in Business at ASU, and that's mostly where the projects below come from.

experience.summary: Build AI-powered tools for the university: a Slack assistant on AWS (Lambda, API Gateway, SQS, DynamoDB) for student/faculty support, and a multimodal LLM-as-a-judge evaluation platform for grading videos, PDFs, and presentations against rubrics. Also write SQL in Redshift for leadership reporting.

Built a license-plate recognition module for an automated gate system using OpenCV and a CNN-based OCR model, and a real estate listing app in Flutter with GraphQL and Firebase, both delivered end-to-end against client specs.

Translated business requirements into user stories, API specs, and UI prototypes for a large-scale mobile money platform, and coordinated UAT and release readiness with engineering and banking partners.

Redesigned a legacy Java payment gateway architecture, cutting code complexity ~90% and authorization time from 60s to 2s. Built Spring Boot APIs used by 20+ financial institutions and led a team of five engineers.

education.detail: GPA 4.0. Coursework: AWS, NLP, Computer Vision, Machine Learning, AI Agents.
GPA 3.82. Coursework: Data Structures & Algorithms, OOP, Database Management.

projects.title: PII Shield
projects.summary: A Chrome extension that masks personal info (emails, SSNs, phone numbers) before it reaches ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini, then unmasks the reply so you still see your real data. Everything runs locally; nothing leaves the browser.

projects.title: ECIN
projects.summary: A credit-scoring platform built on a bronze/silver/gold data pipeline: raw transactions get normalized, turned into features, and served through both a batch training path and a real-time FastAPI scoring endpoint.

projects.title: ASU FaceID
projects.summary: A face-recognition access control system for room entry: a FastAPI backend running ArcFace embeddings, paired with a Next.js admin frontend to enroll faces and review verification logs.

projects.title: AI Slack Connector
projects.summary: A serverless Slack bot that answers questions in-channel using an LLM. Built on AWS SAM: API Gateway and Lambda receive events, SQS queues them, and DynamoDB tracks per-project config so one deployment can serve multiple workspaces.

projects.title: LLM Conversation Semantic Search
projects.summary: A Streamlit proof of concept that anonymizes chat logs with Presidio, embeds them into ChromaDB, and lets you semantically search across a whole conversation history. An exploration of what's possible once chat data becomes searchable.

projects.title: 8-Week SQL Challenge
projects.summary: My solutions to Danny Ma's #8WeekSQLChallenge: real-world case studies in food tech, finance, and marketing, each with its own schema and query set. Mostly here to keep my SQL sharp.
